spec.name: Eviction game board
spec.purpose: The firm's hand-drawn Unlawful Detainer Game Board as an interactive board: every square of the eviction process, the five path types between them, what each move means and what can follow it. Public teaching tool as much as a staff reference - a tenant can read the whole procedure without an account.
layout: GameBoard (SVG board: phase regions, squares, paths, minimap)
BoardKey (KEY: five paths as filters, shapes)
NodeDetail drawer (phase, square kind, who moves, what this means, documents, next moves, how you get here)
logic: Squares, paths, phases and the KEY come from docs/game-board/nodes.json, verified square by square against the poster on 2026-09-20 (docs/game-board/verification-2026-09-20.md); positions are computed by a deterministic serpentine layout (phase regions in a grid, nodes in topological order inside a region), so no coordinate is hand-placed (RULE-BOARD-01).

Square shape follows the poster: document = rounded rectangle, hearing / decision = circle, outcome or event = pill, START is its own square. Outcome and event tones are derived from the path types that reach them, never from an opinion.

Path colour follows the poster's KEY (normal amber, positive green, negative red, neutral slate, jump violet dashed); paths marked reconstructed: true are drawn with a finer dash and the drawer says the firm must confirm them (RULE-BOARD-02).
Phase chips fit the view to one phase region; the search matches labels and notes and opens the square it finds.
Turning a path type off in the KEY hides those paths so the board can be read without them.
The toolbar d-pad, the arrow keys and board.pan move the same view, so the board pans without a pointer and without a drag (P-03, P-04).

Labels hide instead of shrinking below legibility when the board is zoomed out; the layout band (phase columns per row) follows the container width, so a phone gets one winding column and a 4K TV the whole poster.

spec.name: Plan board
spec.purpose: The build plan of CTL OS itself as a board: four columns (Backlog, Doing, Blocked, Done), swimlanes by lane or pass, filters, and a move that writes through the data provider so it survives a reload and a second viewer.
layout: StatTiles (tasks, done, plan length in ticks, critical path)
Filter bar (search, pass, model, lane) + grouping switch
logic: Ticks are dependency depth, not calendar days (D-013): tick(t) = 0 without dependencies, else 1 + max(tick(dep)).
Critical path = every task whose depth + forward height equals the plan span (the longest dependency chain).
A card is blocked-flagged when any dependency is not done; the flag is recomputed on every status write, never read stale.
Moving a card calls DataProvider.update(plan_tasks, id, { status }) and re-derives blocked_by_ids for its dependents.
Reset to repo plan re-applies docs/plan/tasks.json over the stored rows.
Filters and the selected task live in the query string, so a view is addressable (P-06).

spec.name: Drafting studio: the draft
spec.purpose: Where the document is actually written: California pleading paper in the middle with 28 numbered lines and a real caption, the outline and the blanks on the left, and on the right the statutes, the precedent, the live recommendations, the client’s own details and the questions we still owe them — with one button that turns those questions into requests the client answers in their app.

logic: The centre is the PleadingPaper organism: blocks rendered with {{variables}} resolved, each block a contentEditable region snapped to the 28-line grid, pagination computed by line count (28 lines a page, ~85 characters a line) so the editor, the print stylesheet and a screenshot break in the same places.

Every edit is written to drafts by id through the provider (never a local array), with word_count recomputed, so a second editor is not silently overwritten and the realtime pass has nothing to undo (P-14).

Blanks resolve one way: resolveVariables() fills what the case, client and order rows know; a person may override any of them; a required blank still empty is highlighted in the form and is the first live recommendation.

Laws: the template's statute_refs are looked up in docs/legal/statute-index.md through parseStatutes(); the search box searches the whole index. Insert writes the exact citation string into the block that has the caret, so the link back to the row never breaks (RULE-DRAFT-02).
Precedent: precedentsFor() scores the library by shared board squares and shared statutes; every card carries the unverified badge and the standing caution (RULE-DRAFT-04).

Recommendations: the template checklist plus liveRecommendations() — unresolved blanks, an incomplete caption, a filing deadline within three days, unverified statutes, unverified precedents, questions picked but not sent, requests still open with the client, whether the client has approved, whether supervisor review is pending, and the word count.

Client: the order, the case, the client's name, phone and preferred language, the parties, the court, the board square, the open client_requests and the count of binder items on the case (documents rows of kind evidence or upload).

Questions: template questions as checkboxes with "why we ask", plus your own. Send to client writes one client_requests row per selected question (kind question or item, prompt, detail, sent_via app, due in 3 days) and stamps the draft_questions row with its id; if the order sits in assigned or details_complete it also moves to gathering_client_details through applyTransition(), so the board, the desk and the client app all agree (RULE-DRAFT-03, RULE-PIPE-07).
An answered question shows the client's answer with "Insert answer", which drops it into the block that has the caret.

Send for client review is offered only from first_draft or attorney_review: it writes the client_requests review row, sets the draft to sent_for_client_review and moves the order to client_review through applyTransition(); a move the pipeline refuses is reported and never written (RULE-PIPE-08).

Request supervisor review moves approved_by_client to supervisor_review. Mark final is offered only while the order is in supervisor_review and only to can('orders.supervise') (RULE-DRAFT-01, RULE-PIPE-04).

Print / PDF is real: the print stylesheet renders each page at Letter with 28 lines, the browser's own print dialogue saves the PDF. The draft status prints in the footer of every page so an unreviewed copy is recognisable.

Zoom (75 / 100 / 125 per cent) is a CSS custom property on the sheet, so the line grid stays aligned; the value is in the URL (?zoom=) and so is the panel tab (?tab=), which makes both addressable for a voice controller (P-06).

Zoom 0.04..2 with buttons, + / - keys, the wheel (anchored on the cursor; Shift+wheel pans), two-finger pinch on touch, Fit all, Fit selection, 100 % and F.

A transparent capture layer covers the body while dragging or resizing and whenever the zoom is under 0.5, so the iframe cannot swallow the gesture; clicking it (or Enter on the window) "enters" the window and hands the page the pointer.

Live iframes are capped (default 8, 4 / 8 / 12 / 20) and chosen by distance from the viewport centre once the view settles; everything else is a wireframe tile with a Load button, and under 0.2 zoom every window is a tile.

Presets: "All pages by surface" shelf-packs every page code into labelled surface groups (canvasLayout.ts); "Per role" gives one row per surface that role can reach, from the routes' own roles arrays (D-048); "Pipeline walkthrough" reads the seeded canvas_layouts row cvl_pipeline_walkthrough and places its windows even when a path is not built yet - the frame then shows whatever that route renders, honestly.

Layouts are canvas_layouts rows (name, owner_user_id, viewport, windows, flows_visible, role_filter) written through the DataProvider by id; the current viewport, windows and toggles also persist per viewer in localStorage ctl.canvas.v2.

Edges use the game board KEY colours (normal, positive, negative, hand-off = the jump colour) with labels at the midpoints and arrowheads, and a cross-role hand-off names the target role.

Step through walks the flow: the current step's window glows, the rest dim, the caption names the step, Fit selection moves the view, Left / Right step and Escape leaves. "Focus on this role" hides every window the role's flow does not touch.
Every window runs as its own role through the iframe hash (?as=&lang=&dev=&theme=&brand=) applied by frameSession.ts inside the frame only, so the canvas never changes your own session.

Picking a device by hand pins it (?pin=1); "Auto" hands control back to the route. A pinned device of a different kind from the route's is labelled "Responsive check", so a client-app demo is never passed off as a desktop product.
Orientation swaps width and height for phone and tablet only.

Pages come from the route manifest, listed under a heading per surface family; choosing one sets the role to that surface's demo role (client for the client app, front desk for the desk, attorney for counsel...). Parameterised paths are filled with the same sample ids the QA scripts use.
Role, language, theme and builder tool are passed through the iframe hash (?as=&dev=&lang=&theme=) and applied inside the frame only (frameSession.ts), so presenting never changes your own session.

Device, pin, page, role, language, theme, rotation, present mode and tour step live in the URL query (?device=&pin=&route=&role=&lang=&theme=&dev=&rot=&present=&step=), so a link reopens the same demo.

The tour is a scripted sequence on the right device each time: hub (laptop), the client's orders on phone 390, the game board, the attorney pipeline on 1920, the owner on 2560, the proposal on a laptop. A step whose page is still being built falls back to the nearest page that exists and says so.

Present mode hides the page chrome and leaves the device, its identity badges and the tour buttons; the keyboard shortcuts show once (remembered in localStorage ctl.simulator). Keyboard: P present, arrows step the tour, D cycles the device, R rotates (phone and tablet only), Esc leaves.

The office-page link goes to caltenantlaw.com (external, new tab), never to an internal route a public visitor is not allowed on (D-048).
